run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The payment-api pod in app-100a (payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-f5tl5, labels job=payment-api, service=payment-api) logged an error burst from 2026-11-20T13:49:24Z to about 14:44:44Z: 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' and 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001) with pool_size 20 and active_connections 20, plus '/healthz' health-check failures answered 503 at 13:57:29, 14:01:50 and 14:44:44. Waiting requests reached 46 and acquisition waits up to 26789 ms. In the same pod's own DEBUG lines, 'Database query executed' durations for 'SELECT * FROM payments WHERE status = ?' were 15-88 ms at 12:30-13:34 and then 1252 ms at 13:50:55 and 2355-4953 ms at 14:28-14:43, so the failure coincided with a large slowdown of the pod's database dependency. Some payments still succeeded during the burst (14:07:40 and 14:09:43), so it was a partial degradation, not a full stop. A 1-hour-window count over the authorized day shows level ERROR only in the windows covering roughly 13:54-14:54, so the burst is distinct from background noise. The database itself is not a workload in this cluster (no postgres/mysql/db pods; the only datastore is otel-demo valkey-cart) and the app script and DB settings come from a secret that cannot be read, so the degraded dependency could not be inspected or named as an object; no root cause object is asserted. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable throughout this run, so no metric or trace evidence, no restart count and no probe events exist for the incident window; the flagd payment fault flags are all at defaultVariant 'off' and target the separate otel-demo payment service, so they are not this cause.

claims.text: The app-100a workload is Deployment payment-api-100a (replicas 1, revision '1', image python:3.9-slim, command /app/app-direct-push.py); container 'payment-api' serves /healthz on 8080 with a livenessProbe of failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 10, timeoutSeconds 10, and mounts volume app-script from a secret (value redacted).

The only pod of that Deployment present at query time is payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-f5tl5: phase Running, all conditions Ready, restartCount 0, empty lastState, container started 2026-11-21T04:29:51Z, owned by ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 which was created 2026-11-21T04:29:50Z; the only other app-100a pod is loki-66445c6d6f-5kpbp (created 2026-11-21T04:29:27Z).

The retained events for app-100a span only 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z to 04:29:51Z and consist of Deployment ScalingReplicaSet x2, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate x2 and Pod Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started x2, with no Warning events; no event from 2026-11-20 is present in the cluster-wide event set (other groups: kube-system Pod Unhealthy x6, otel-demo Pod BackOff x2 and Unhealthy x4, local-path-storage BackOff x1).

First observed failure in the payment-api log stream is at 2026-11-20T13:49:24Z: level ERROR, message 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted', pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 27, wait_time_ms 17653; a query of all ERROR lines from 12:00:00Z to 13:50:00Z returned only that line.

Between 13:45:00Z and 15:00:00Z the pod logged 16 lines containing 'database': 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' (pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests 7-46, wait_time_ms 5216-26789) and 'Health check failed - database unreachable' with endpoint /healthz, status_code 503, response_time_ms 5009-9684 at 13:57:29, 14:01:50 and 14:44:44; the same stream carries 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' with error_code DB_CONN_001 and stack 'at PaymentService.processPayment() / at DatabasePool.acquire()'.

The pod's own 'Database query executed' DEBUG lines for 'SELECT * FROM payments WHERE status = ?' report duration_ms 30 at 12:30:17, 61 at 12:32:58, 18 at 13:06:28, 88 at 13:17:12, 15 at 13:20:57, 65 at 13:34:45, then 1252 at 13:50:55, 3106 at 14:28:27, 4953 at 14:30:57, 4472 at 14:37:32 and 2355 at 14:43:57.

A 1-hour-window count_over_time by level across the authorized day (evaluation 2026-11-20T05:33:30Z to 2026-11-21T04:28:30Z) returns level ERROR points only for the windows ending approximately 2026-11-20T13:54Z through 14:54Z (values 1 rising to 22 per hour window), while level INFO and DEBUG series exist across the day.

Successful business activity continued inside the burst: 'Payment processed successfully' INFO lines at 13:31:51 (PAY-9343, 468 ms), 14:07:40 (PAY-5221, 389 ms) and 14:09:43 (PAY-3838, 323 ms), alongside ERROR entries in the same stream.

No database workload exists in this cluster to inspect: pods matching postgres|mysql|mongo|redis|valkey|database|db- across all namespaces are only otel-demo valkey-cart-d6456b5b6-5dlsx (valkey/valkey:7.2-alpine), frontend-proxy-844799bcdb-pv5mn and shipping-6fc5f694db-9sq2c; the only StatefulSet is otel-demo/alertmanager; namespace app-100a exposes only the loki Service (ClusterIP 10.96.120.224:3100) and its ConfigMaps are kube-root-ca.crt and loki-config.

The only ConfigMap cluster-wide whose name or data keys match payment|fault|inject|chaos|flagd is otel-demo/flagd-config; in it paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') are state ENABLED but defaultVariant 'off', and every other flag (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) also has defaultVariant 'off'.

Loki counts grouped by namespace over 12:00:00Z-15:00:00Z returned series only for namespace app-100a (levels DEBUG, ERROR, INFO); no otel-demo namespace log series was returned, so other services' logs were not available to assess.

The proximate cause of the payment-api errors is degradation of its database dependency: the same pod's DB query durations rose from 15-88 ms (12:30-13:34) to 1252 ms at 13:50:55 and 2355-4953 ms (14:28-14:43), the app reports 'database unreachable' on /healthz, and 20 of 20 pool connections stayed busy with 7-46 queued requests, i.e. slow DB calls held connections until the pool was exhausted. The database endpoint and its own health are outside what this evidence covers.

A second candidate is a request-volume surge against payment-api: waiting_requests rose to 46 and queue waits to 26789 ms. No request-rate, load-generator or span metric is available in this run to test whether offered load increased, so this remains unverified.

The flagd fault-injection flags were considered and rejected as the cause of this pod's errors: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are at defaultVariant 'off', and flagd-config lives in otel-demo and describes failing the otel-demo 'payment' service, a different identity from app-100a's payment-api Deployment and its job=payment-api/service=payment-api labels.

A crash or OOM explanation is not supported by the objects as they stand: the present payment-api container has restartCount 0 with empty lastState and the pod is Ready, and the retained app-100a events contain no OOMKilled, Evicted or BackOff reason; this describes only the pod created 2026-11-21T04:29:50Z, not the pod that logged on 2026-11-20.

Decouple the liveness probe from the database: /healthz returns 503 when the DB is unreachable and the Deployment uses failureThreshold 3 / periodSeconds 10, so a DB stall of tens of seconds can kill an otherwise functional pod; use a dependency-free liveness endpoint, express DB availability as readiness, and consider larger probe thresholds.

Instrument the DB dependency directly in Prometheus (connection-acquire latency, active/waiting pool gauges, query-duration histogram), because pool_size 20 saturation and multi-second query latency are currently visible only as unstructured log lines.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for every attempt in this run (get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query and traces_search all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no metric series (e.g. traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_*_duration*, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total) and no trace spans exist for the 2026-11-20 13:45 window; restart counts, error rates and latency trends for that time are unknown, not zero.

The pod's database dependency could not be investigated: no database workload or Service exists in the cluster, and the app script and DB settings are mounted from a secret (volume app-script) that cannot be read, so the DB host, its health and the pool_size 20 setting could not be verified.

Events are retained only for 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z-04:29:51Z, so there is no event evidence of restarts, liveness-probe failures, OOMKilled or Evicted for the incident-era pod; whether it restarted during the burst is unknown.

The incident-era pod identity is unresolved: the 2026-11-20 log lines carry pod_name payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-f5tl5, but that pod now has creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T04:29:50Z with restartCount 0 and the Deployment revision is still '1'; the reason for that discrepancy is unknown.

A log query for app-100a ERROR lines from 2026-11-20T14:50:00Z to 16:30:00Z returned no data (status no_data), and a fetch of the current container's logs over 2026-11-21T03:30:47Z-04:30:47Z returned no lines (status no_data, previous instance not found); these empty results show only that those queries matched nothing, not proof of absence.
No NetworkPolicy objects were returned (status no_data), so connectivity policy as a cause could not be confirmed or excluded.
Change history is not an integrated source in this run, so no change record exists for the app-100a workload or its database around 2026-11-20 13:45.
Impact beyond this pod is unverified: Loki returned no otel-demo namespace log series for 12:00-15:00Z, so callers of payment-api and wider customer impact could not be checked.

The later state change in the window (app-100a, kube-system and otel-demo objects created around 2026-11-21T04:29Z with Deployment revision still 1) cannot be attributed to this incident; it is recorded as a change of unknown cause after the error burst.
next_steps: Repair or re-enable the Prometheus and Jaeger integrations, then re-query 2026-11-20 13:30-15:00 for kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total, traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} and any app_payment_* series to quantify restart count, error rate and transaction impact.

Identify the database endpoint and credentials used by payment-api (with the owning team; the secret is not readable here) and review that database's slow-query and connection-limit telemetry for 2026-11-20 13:45-14:55.
Review the payment-api connection-pool configuration and the liveness probe coupling to /healthz with the owning team before any change.
Check whether the app-100a environment was rebuilt around 2026-11-21T04:29Z and whether that incidentally ended or masked the condition.
